name: RH Scheduler Mediator
description: Read-only mutual-availability, slot-proposal, and conflict checks brokered by Redesign Health's scheduler-mediator service, without exposing either side's raw calendar to the calling agent.

methods.whenToUse: Use for any Redesign Health EA agent that negotiates scheduling with another person's calendar. This is an RH-internal service reachable only over the RH tailnet -- there is no public sign-up or OAuth flow, so it is provisioned once per Paperclip instance by RH platform engineering, not connected per-company by an operator pasting a key.

credentialFields.label: rh-scheduler-mcp bearer token
credentialFields.placeholder: rh-auth JWT for the calling EA agent's service identity
credentialFields.helperMd: This is deliberately NOT a single shared, static company API key the way most `api_key` connectors use this field. `rh-scheduler-mcp`'s tools take an explicit `bearer_token` per call and resolve caller identity from it per request (see its `server.py` module docstring: 'whose calendar' and 'who's asking' must both come from the call, never from ambient/process identity, because one deployment serves every Paperclip EA agent). Modeling this as one static `company_secrets` credential is a known interim simplification -- see the connector proposal's Transport And Auth notes for what a real per-agent-identity token mint would require instead.

methods.guidanceMd: Reachable only from inside RH's Tailscale tailnet (ECS task + `tailscale` sidecar per `terraform/main.tf`; no ALB, no public IP). Connect this once per Paperclip instance as a platform-provisioned connection, not per company. All 4 tools are read-only in the current shadow-mode deployment (TECH-4878); there is no booking or send path to gate.
warnings: The bearer-token credential field models a single static token, but the real server expects the token's JWT subject to match the calling identity on every request; a shared token means every call is attributed to one identity regardless of which EA agent actually made it. Do not treat this as solved -- it is flagged here for the follow-up that gives each EA agent (or each requesting company) its own minted rh-auth JWT.

The MCP server exposes no write/booking/send tools today (shadow-mode, read-only). Do not configure this connection with any ask-first write policy as if a write action exists -- there is none to gate.
